speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned waking up frightened; can you tell me if you have been having any nightmares or night terrors, and do you remember the dreams at all? Also, have you noticed any heavy breathing or gasping during sleep?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Night Terrors (Sleep Terrors)

Based on the history of episodes where the child yells and cries but is not confused afterward and can be consoled quickly, these features are inconsistent with typical nightmares or night terrors. Can you confirm if these episodes occur primarily during the first third of the night, and have you noticed any sudden increase in heart rate or sweating during these events? REQUEST TEST: Sleep-Study (Polysomnography)
